clue.text: Such a mug is Ron, anyhow

definitions.text: Such a mug is Ron, anyhow

indicators.note: anyhow means in any old way, carelessly, so the letters of the words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark that someone called Ron is a real fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyhow' rearranges the letters of A MUG IS RON, and the whole clue then describes the result: Ron is that kind of mug.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug is a fool, and an ignorant person is exactly that sort of dupe.

clue.text: Unsuitable paint mix

indicators.note: to mix is to stir together, so the letters of paint are rearranged

explanation.surface: Complaining that a paint blend is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means inappropriate or ill-fitting.

clue.text: Indifferent — neither forward nor backward

definitions.meaning: the gear position of a car that is in no drive gear

explanation.surface: Someone apathetic who will not go either way.
explanation.definitionFit: Impartial in a dispute; also the gearbox setting between drive and reverse.

clue.text: Russian pelt found on board -

definitions.note: board is a dining table, where this vegetable or condiment appears

parts.note: red is a traditional label for a Soviet Russian
to pepper is to pelt with shot or missiles

explanation.surface: A Russian fur coat discovered aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pelt' looks like an animal skin, but it is the verb; 'board' is the old word for a dining table.
explanation.definitionFit: Capsicums and the hot spice are served at table, the board of an old feast.

clue.text: Annoyance with doctor taking the foreign post

parts.note: MO is a medical officer
le is the in French
a station is a post, as in a duty station

explanation.surface: A doctor irritated at being posted abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Molestation is harassment, persistent pestering.

clue.text: Exactly like this Italian agreement about …

parts.note: si is Italian for yes
c is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: An Italian saying yes to something, then trailing off.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots run this clue on into 6 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Sic, Latin for thus, marks a quotation as reproduced word for word.

clue.text: Transport the French Line

parts.note: a cab is a form of transport
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A heading about French transport, as if naming a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable is a thick rope or wire, a kind of line.

clue.text: … many a hot spot for witches

definitions.note: the answer is a gathering of these, not a single one

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
an oven is a hot place

explanation.surface: Continuing from 5 down: lots of hot places for witches.
explanation.definitionFit: A coven is an assembly of thirteen or so practitioners of witchcraft.

clue.text: Sticker cut short in the plant

parts.note: a bur is a prickly seed head that sticks to clothing
to dock is to cut short, as a tail

explanation.surface: A clinging seed snipped off a garden plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' looks like it trims BURR, but it is DOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Burdock is a large weed with clinging burs.

clue.text: Points to imprisonment causing suffering

parts.note: E and N are compass points
durance is an old word for imprisonment

explanation.surface: Aiming someone towards prison causes hardship.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is the bearing of hardship, putting up with pain.

clue.text: Castle has a ladder of the Spanish kind

parts.note: a ladder in tights is a run
del is Spanish for of the

explanation.surface: A castle with a ladder in some Spanish style.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladder here is the British word for a run in stockings. ARUNDEL Castle is a famous castle in West Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Arundel is a well-known English castle, home of the Dukes of Norfolk.

clue.text: Overlay, finished in last month, turned back

indicators.note: in places the word for finished inside the other piece
turned back means the abbreviation for the last month is read in reverse order

parts.note: December, abbreviated Dec, is the last month of the year
over means finished, done

explanation.surface: Some overlay work, completed at the end of December, then turned around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned back' makes CED (the month abbreviation backwards); 'in' then splits it after its first letter. 'Overlay' must be read as a participle-like description, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlay something is to cover it, so a thing laid over is covered; the clue uses the participle sense.

clue.text: Buckler's great disaster

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: a disaster wrecks things, so the letters of the word great are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A man named Buckler suffers a terrible calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: Buckler looks like a surname, but a buckler is a small shield.
explanation.definitionFit: A targe is a small round shield, the same sort of light shield as a buckler.

clue.text: Records played back finish our brilliant display

indicators.note: played back means the word for records is reversed, as a tape is rewound

parts.note: LPs are long-playing records
end means finish
taken as written

explanation.surface: Playing old records backwards ends our impressive show.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendour is magnificence, a dazzling show of grandeur.

clue.text: Various alien lines going to the East in formation

indicators.note: various means assorted, so the letters of alien are rearranged

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the railway lines
taken as written

explanation.surface: Assorted alien lines heading eastward in formation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' turns ALIEN into LINEA. BR stands for British Rail.
explanation.definitionFit: Line abreast is a naval or flying formation of ships or aircraft side by side.

clue.text: Sounds like everything a cobbler needs

indicators.note: sounds like signals that the word for everything is said aloud, giving a same-sounding word

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A claim that a shoemaker needs everything.
explanation.definitionFit: An awl is the pointed tool a shoemaker uses to pierce leather.

clue.text: Is a landau broken down in Spain?

indicators.note: broken down means the carriage is wrecked, so its letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Asks whether a carriage has failed on a Spanish road.
explanation.definitionFit: Andalusia is a southern region of the Iberian kingdom, with Seville and Granada.

clue.text: Calling a spade a spade near Salisbury?

definitions.meaning: describes someone blunt and direct in speech
jokingly, voiced on the open land beside Salisbury in Wiltshire

explanation.surface: A frank speaker who lives near Salisbury.
explanation.walkthrough: Salisbury Plain is a large chalk plateau in Wiltshire, England, so the second reading splits the answer into Plain and spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Blunt, outspoken people speak frankly; the second sense is talking on the Wiltshire plateau.

clue.text: Summary a Scot made — very nice chap

parts.note: a precis is a summary
Ian is a common Scottish name

explanation.surface: A Scot writes a summary about a pleasant fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice here means exact, fastidious, not pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A precisian is a punctilious person, strict about exact rules.

clue.text: Fixed two consecutive notes to end

parts.note: D and E are neighbouring notes of the musical scale
to terminate is to end

explanation.surface: Settling the last two notes of a tune before it finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Notes are the letters A to G, so two in a row can be D and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Determinate means settled and definite, with set limits.

clue.text: Poor nag in temporary accommodation — touching

indicators.note: in puts the reworked horse inside the shelter

parts.note: a tent is a temporary shelter

indicators.note: poor means in bad shape, so the letters of nag are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sad old horse sheltered in a tent, which is moving.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangent line meets a curve at one point, just making contact.

clue.text: Goddess took nourishment

definitions.meaning: The Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A deity having a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ate is the Greek spirit of folly; also the past tense of eating, consuming food.

clue.text: Articles first written by an unbeliever

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
the is the definite article
1st written with I for the figure one

explanation.surface: Newspaper articles first penned by a sceptic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first written' signals 1ST written with the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An atheist denies the existence of God.

clue.text: Poet includes new bits for the squire

indicators.note: includes means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: Walter Savage Landor was an English poet

indicators.note: in bits means broken into pieces, so the letters of new are scrambled

explanation.surface: A poet works fresh fragments into a portrait of a country squire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bits' scrambles the word new, giving WNE, and 'includes' sets that inside the poet's surname. Walter Savage Landor was a nineteenth-century English poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A squire was a country gentleman who owned an estate.

clue.text: Less fashionable hit?

definitions.meaning: in archery or shooting, a strike on the outermost ring of a target

explanation.surface: Asking whether an unfashionable song was a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of out, unfashionable; also a shot landing in the outermost target ring.

clue.text: Watery humour from an Ipswich orphan

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A tearful story from a Suffolk orphan.
explanation.walkthrough: Ipswich is a town in Suffolk; humour here is an old word for a body fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: Ichor is a thin watery discharge from a wound, one of the body's fluids.

clue.text: Concerning journalist's instruments

parts.note: re means concerning, about
ed is short for editor, a journalist, with the 's

explanation.surface: About the tools of a reporter's trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeds are woodwind instruments, or the vibrating parts in them.

clue.text: Automatic eminence for Greek: herald

parts.note: a Sten is an automatic gun
a tor is a rocky hill, an eminence

explanation.surface: Machine-gun fire from a hilltop for a Greek warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: TOR is a rocky hill on Dartmoor and similar uplands.
explanation.definitionFit: Stentor was the loud-voiced herald of the Greeks in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Perch caught with it?

definitions.meaning: an old unit of length, also called a pole
what a fish is caught with, an angler's pole

explanation.surface: Asking whether a perch was landed with a fishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perch' looks like the fish, which is what makes the second half seem to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod is an old measure of five and a half yards, and also a fishing pole.

clue.text: Miss Oakley's occupation, you say? How colourful!

indicators.note: you say means the words are pronounced, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: Annie Oakley was the sharpshooter, and a line is an occupation

explanation.surface: Asking what Annie Oakley did for a living and marvelling at the colours.
explanation.walkthrough: Annie's line (of work) said aloud gives the dye name.
explanation.definitionFit: Aniline is the compound used to make bright synthetic dyes.

clue.text: A man of parts

parts.note: a man of parts is a talented man, but here it is one who plays roles on stage

explanation.definitionFit: A performer takes parts in plays, so he is literally a man of parts.

clue.text: Sets off for school among the fruit trees

indicators.note: among means the school is placed inside the trees

parts.note: date palms bear dates
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Leaving for school through an orchard.
explanation.definitionFit: Detonates means explodes, as one triggers a bomb.
